newsitem.title: UK: Symonds says discovers breach of controls.
newsitem.headline: Symonds says discovers breach of controls.

text.p: British engineering group Symonds Plc said on Monday that it had discovered siginificant breaches of internal controls within its Precision Engineering division after it conducted a detailed internal management review.
The company said it now expected its group's pre-tax profits for the first quarter of 1997 to be lower than it forecast in its March 25 trading update.
The share price of Symonds fell 8-1/2pence to 38- 1/2 moments after it made this announcement.
"The directors believe that the management accounts for the Precision Engineering division do not accurately reflect the performance of the division for the first quarter of 1997," the company said.
"The directors therefore expect that the group's profit before taxation will be lower than that expected at the time of the trading update," it added.
The group had warned on March 25 that it had experienced a difficult first quarter in 1997 due to tough market conditions.
The group also sacked Ken Garner, the managing director of Precision Engineering, who has been replaced by Patrick Curren.
Arthur Andersen & Co is currently investigating the breaches and will submit a detailed report to the board in three weeks.
